en: The amihan brings cool, dry northeast winds to the Philippines between November and February.
The habagat or southwest monsoon causes heavy rainfall across western parts of the Philippines.
The town of Bolinao in Pangasinan produces white marble, a metamorphic rock formed from limestone.
Miners extract large amounts of gold from the volcanic rocks found in Masbate province.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is a perfect cone-shaped stratovolcano formed by layers of hardened lava and ash.
The Philippine Fault Zone is a major fracture in the Earth's crust that causes local earthquakes.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Farmers near Taal Volcano grow vegetables and coconuts because volcanic ash creates highly fertile soil.
The Philippines launched Diwata-2, a microsatellite built to monitor weather and natural disasters from space.
The moon's gravitational pull creates the high and low tides observed in Manila Bay.
El Nino causes severe droughts in the Philippines by warming the Pacific Ocean surface waters.
Zambales province contains large deposits of chromite, a dark mineral used to make stainless steel.
